Five points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The downgrade direction conflicts with Kenanga's own earlier note. This report is headed MARKET PERFORM with a down arrow and says it is 'adjusting our call from OUTPERFORM to MARKET PERFORM', but Kenanga's Plastic Packaging sector update of 15 July 2026 had already downgraded 'SCIENTX (MP, TP: RM3.91) from OUTPERFORM to MARKET PERFORM following share price action' - at the same RM3.91 target. Between the two, the peer tables in Kenanga's own TGUAN and BPPLAS results notes of 27 August show SCIENTEX BHD as OP at RM3.70/RM3.91, and no note upgrading it back to OUTPERFORM was publicly retrievable. The two documents cannot both be right; both are recorded here. (2) The segmental table does not add up in its full-year columns. Packaging plus Property gives FY26 turnover of RM4,813.0m and FY25 of RM4,517.7m - matching the Results Highlights table and the company's own filing - but the Group Turnover row prints RM3,657.9m and RM3,408.3m. The same happens on EBIT: the segments sum to RM881.5m for FY26 and RM742.1m for FY25 against printed group figures of RM677.2m and RM565.2m. The quarterly columns in the same table do reconcile. (3) The Summary Earnings Table's valuation ratios appear struck at a lower share price than the RM3.70 on the cover - Core PER of 8.6x/8.8x/8.5x on core EPS of 40.2/39.4/40.8 sen implies about RM3.46-3.47, and PBV of 1.2x on BVPS of RM2.9 implies about RM3.48, while the page 5 peer table shows 9.4x and 9.1x at RM3.70. That implied price is arithmetic on the report's own numbers and is inferred, not stated. (4) The sum-of-parts table divides by 1,551m paid-up shares while the stock information box gives 1,556.3m shares outstanding, and takes the property segment at RM4,598m against the RM4,602m discounted RNAV computed in the following table. (5) The rating-definition box on page 6 defines OUTPERFORM and OVERWEIGHT as expected total return 'MORE than 1 %', where the same day's Kenanga Today prints 'MORE than 10%'.

This is an Initiate Coverage report; it is filed here as a Company Update because this board's report-type dropdown is fixed to five types (rules/signals.md §6). There is no previous rating or previous target price, by definition. Four points of caution on the figures, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The report gives two different sets of WFE-exposure numbers. Page 1 says AMBEST's wafer-fab-equipment exposure is ‘projected to rise from approximately 47% of revenue in FY24 to some 70% by FY26’; page 8 says it will be ‘propelled from ~53% in FY2024 to ~76% by FY2027’, above an exhibit titled ‘We Estimate Ambest's WFE-Related Order to Account for ~65%/76% of Revenue in FY26/FY27’. FY24 appears as both 47% and 53%, FY26 as both 70% and 65%. The Edge Malaysia's 11 September report of this note carries the page-1 pair. (2) The financial year-end is labelled two ways. The front Summary Earnings Table says ‘FYE Dec’ and the page 13 peer table says ‘Current FYE 12/2026’, while the income statement, balance sheet, cash flow and ratio tables on page 12 all say ‘FYE May’. December is the reading the rest of the document supports - FY25 turnover of RM52.7m matches the trailing-twelve-month revenue on the market-data source, and 1HFY26 is already reported - but the note is not internally consistent and states no correction. (3) The front table's per-share figures are struck off a different profit line from the peer table's. The Summary Earnings Table shows FY26F Core EPS of 2.5 sen and Core PER of 60.1x, which at RM1.48 is FY26F net profit of RM12.6m over 510.0m shares; the FY26F core net profit of RM16.1m in the same column gives about 3.2 sen and about 47x on the same share base - and the peer table duly prints 3.0 sen and 49.0x. That reconciliation is arithmetic on the report's own numbers and is inferred, not stated. (4) The page 12 income statement has two row labels transposed: the ‘Associate’ row carries the PBT figures (9.0 / 8.2 / 7.5 / 16.6 / 46.0) and the ‘Exceptional Items’ row carries the taxation figures (2.2 / 1.1 / 1.1 / 4.1 / 9.4), each duplicating the correctly labelled row beneath it. The company is also named three ways in the same document - ‘AMBEST Berhad’ in the page headers, ‘AMBEST GROUP BHD’ in the peer table and ‘Ambest Precision Engineering Sdn. Bhd.’ in the company overview; the listed entity is Ambest Group Berhad.

Page 1 says ‘We like IOICORP (OP; TP: RM5.40) and KLK (OP; TP:RM25.80) for the larger planters’; page 2 says ‘Our picks include IOICORP (OP; TP:RM5.40) for strong FY27 prospects...’. Eleven points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The bear-case de-rating for MAXIS is stated two ways. Page 1 says CDB’s asymmetric risk-reward holds ‘despite a more punitive bear case de-rating of -3SD (MAXIS: -2SD)’; pages 5 to 7 apply -1SD to MAXIS three times (‘for MAXIS... we assume a de-rating to -1SD’; ‘a de-rating to -1SD at 17.0x P/E’; ‘a de-rating to 17x (historical -1SD level)’). The -1SD reading is the one the rest of the document supports, since 17.0x is what produces the RM2.82/RM2.83 bear-case value. (2) MAXIS’s position against its own historical mean is stated two ways. Page 1: ‘it already trades at historical mean’. Page 5: ‘MAXIS, which is currently trading below its historical mean’. Page 6 gives 18.1x against a 19.7x mean, which is below it. (3) MAXIS’s bear-case value is printed twice at two figures - RM2.82 on page 6 and RM2.83 on page 7, both at 17.0x and both described as 20% downside; Exhibit 15 gives RM2.83. (4) The SWN announcement is dated two ways. Exhibit 1 and the page-2 text both put it in Mar 2021, but page 3 says MAXIS ‘remains 24% below its Sept-21 level, when SWN was first announced’. (5) MAXIS’s RM500m-scenario debt headroom does not match its own exhibit. The text gives RM3.01b; Exhibit 20 prints RM3,068m, which is also what RM3,568m less RM500m gives. The CDB equivalents reconcile exactly (RM1,546m/RM1,846m/RM2,046m against RM1.55b/RM1.85b/RM2.05b). (6) The 2026 DNB cash-commitment total does not add up from its own components. The text says ‘total annual cash commitments related to DNB in 2026 totalled RM528m p.a.’ while naming RM202m of April 2026 shareholders’ advances and RM328m for the MoF put option, which sum to RM530m (RM529.9m on Exhibit 16’s RM327.9m). (7) The headline scenario percentages are rounded in the text and precise in the exhibit: CDB +37%/-26% against Exhibit 13’s +36.6%/(25.5%), MAXIS +21%/-20% against +20.9%/(20.3%). (8) Exhibit 12’s caption contradicts the text - it reads ‘Bear −1SD / Bull: Hist. mean P/E’ for both stocks, though the text applies -3SD to CDB’s bear case. (9) CDB’s FY27F EPS appears as three figures: 12.7 sen in Exhibit 14’s 0% row, ‘13 sen’ in the stress-test text, and 12.8 sen in the peer table’s two-year forward core EPS. Related: the bear-case values cannot be reproduced from the stated multiple and base-case EPS alone - RM2.02 at 18.8x implies about 10.7 sen - because the bear case also assumes lower earnings; the note states the de-rating but never prints its bear-case EPS. That gap is identified here, not in the report. (10) The peer table’s price snapshot predates the same day’s digest. It shows AXIATA at RM1.68 and TELEKOM MALAYSIA at RM8.00, while Kenanga Today’s 11 September closes are RM1.71 and RM7.92. CDB’s RM2.72 and MAXIS’s RM3.54, used as ‘current share price’ throughout the note, do not appear in the digest’s tables and so could not be cross-checked. (11) Two sections are both numbered ‘(V)’, and this is filed as a Sector Update although the document is headed ‘Thematic Report’, because this board’s report-type dropdown is fixed to five types (rules/signals.md §6). It carries no ticker-level rating, target price or share price of its own, so those columns are empty by design. The divergence marker is deliberately not set: named houses do rate MAXIS opposite to Kenanga (see the analyst note), but this row carries no Kenanga rating of its own against which §3’s opposite-direction test can be applied.

Five points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The peer average behind the target price cannot be reproduced from the report's own table. The TP is set at 37x FY27F PER, stated as a 10% discount to the average FY27 PER of 41.3x for local semiconductor front-end peers named as UWC, Frontken and Vitrox. But VITROX does not appear anywhere in the Malaysian Technology Peers Comparison on page 3, and the two named peers that do appear show two-year forward core PERs of 39.3x (UWC) and 31.7x (FRONTKEN), which average 35.5x rather than 41.3x. The 41.3x is therefore drawn from a peer set the document does not print. (2) KGB's own ROE is given two ways. The Financial Data & Ratios table on page 2 shows FY26F ROE of 24.5% and FY27F of 27.1%; the peer table on page 3 shows 27.8% for the one-year forward period, which every other column in that row (core EPS 21.7 sen, PBV 9.7x, net dividend 15.0 sen, yield 1.7%) identifies as FY26F. (3) The exchange rate implied by the contract conversion is not the one in the same day's digest. USD249.9m as c.RM1.01b and USD202.0m as c.RM817m both imply about RM4.04 to the dollar, against the 14 September USD/MYR fix of 4.0753 printed in Kenanga Today the same morning. The report carries no note on share issuance, warrant conversion or dilution. This divergence is identified here, not in the report. (5) The 52-week range in Kenanga's own stock-information box (H RM9.20, L RM4.75) differs from the market data used in this row's range columns (stockanalysis.com: RM9.25 / RM4.70).

Seven points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The day's published bundle is two reports short of the day's advertised line-up. Both the digest's Ideas of the Day and Kenanga's own Kenanga Today page for 18 September name Economic Viewpoint: Bond Market Weekly Outlook, Ringgit Weekly Outlook alongside this Company Update and a Rating Summary - but the published bundle contains only the digest and this report. Both Economic Viewpoints returned HTTP 404 under every filename convention this board knows, including the exact patterns that worked for the same two titles on 28 August, 4 September and 7 September. They are excluded on the authority of the bundle contents, the same treatment given BIMB on 27 August. Rating Summary is excluded by specification. This day therefore carries one report row, not three. (2) The headline discount is measured against book value, but the text applies it to the market. Exhibit 1 compares realisable value of RM1,358.0m to a PPE carrying value of RM961.8m for a discount of 29.2% - which reconciles exactly. The text, however, says the market 'currently prices the stock at a 30% discount' and that 'the market is mispricing the company by 29.2% based on its fleet's realizable value alone'. Market capitalisation is RM1,083.0m in the note's own Stock Information box, which against RM1,358.0m is a 20.3% discount, not 29.2% - arithmetic here, and identified here rather than in the document. (3) The payback claim does not reconcile to the PPE figure used elsewhere in the note. The text states that on FY26F earnings of RM72m the group 'would be able to breakeven on its PPE value in 12 years'.
